title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a handwritten sheet on the verso of a typescript of a Bourbaki-style analysis text (holomorphic functions, the prolongement analytique chapter). The Grothendieck material is a fragment from the 1965 'Galois theory of motives' notes about 'catégories de Dedekind' over a commutative base A (a Dedekind ring or scheme).

(1) Picard-type invariant. For a Dedekind category C over A with extra datum τ, one has a 'Pordet(C,τ)'. The best reading is a Picard category of invertible (A-linear) objects or autoequivalences of C. Its π_0 sits in an exact sequence
0 → Pic(S or A) → π_0 Pordet(C,τ) → Ram(C/A) → 0.
Here Ram(C/A) := Pordet(C)/Pic(A) ≅ ⊕_p Z/e_p(C)Z, where e_p(C) is the ramification index of C at the prime p.

This is exactly the categorical form of a classical fact. For a maximal (or hereditary) order Λ in a central simple algebra over a Dedekind domain, the invertible two-sided ideals modulo ideals of A form ⊕_p Z/e_p, because P^{e_p} = pΛ. So a 'Dedekind category' is the abstract, Morita-invariant version of the category of modules over such an order: an A-linear abelian category locally Morita-equivalent to modules over hereditary orders. The local invariants e_p are its ramification.

(2) Forms and torsors. Take a commutative A-algebra A', a Dedekind category C' over A', and an object T' (in some H_{A'}(C')). Suppose (C_{A'}, T_{A'}) is locally isomorphic to (C', T'); it suffices, e.g., that C_{A'} ≅ C' and Pic(A') = 0, for instance A' local. Then the equivalences (φ,u) form a category. Here φ: C_{A'} → C' is an A'-linear admissible equivalence and u: φ(T_{A'}) ≅ T'. This category is a bitorsor: under Eq(C_{A'},T_{A'}) acting on the right and Eq(C',T') acting on the left.

(3) Unramified case. If Ram(C'/A') = 0 (C' unramified, i.e. Azumaya-like), the equivalence category is a torsor under the Picard category Tors(C', G_m). There is a canonical equivalence Eq(C_{A'},T_{A'}) ≅ Eq(C',T') of Picard categories, so the left and right torsor structures should identify. Grothendieck marks this 'À vérifier !!'.

Purpose: a descent and forms theory of A-linear categories (Morita/Brauer theory). In the motivic context it presumably describes the band, or fibre-functor torsors, for 'Galois groups' of categories of motives over arithmetic bases, where ramification of the coefficient category matters.
errors: The final identification of the left and right torsor structures is flagged by Grothendieck himself as 'À vérifier !!'. In general a bitorsor under two Picard categories gives such an identification only up to the inner/conjugation action. For the Picard (commutative) band Tors(C',G_m) it is plausible but needs the braiding/symmetry to be compatible.
Line 2 writes 'Pic(S)' while elsewhere the base is A; this is a notational inconsistency (S = Spec A presumably).
The interlinear hypothesis reads '(C', A')' where it should evidently read '(C', T')'.

ideas.what: Dedekind category over a Dedekind base, with local ramification indices e_p(C) and Ram(C/A) = Pic-type group / Pic(A) ≅ ⊕ Z/e_p Z
ideas.modern_name: Hereditary/maximal orders up to Morita equivalence; equivalently coherent sheaves on a stacky (root-stack) curve, where Pic(root stack)/Pic(curve) ≅ ⊕ Z/e_p
ideas.usually_credited_to: Auslander–Goldman, Reiner (maximal orders, 1960s–70s); stacky viewpoint: Chan–Ingalls, Lieblich, Artin–de Jong (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as far as known; the Brauer group papers (Dix exposés) treat Azumaya algebras, not ramified orders categorically

ideas.what: Exact sequence 0 → Pic(A) → π_0(Picard category of C) → Ram(C/A) → 0
ideas.modern_name: Picard group of an order / of an orbifold curve modulo Pic of the coarse space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for orders (Fröhlich, Reiner); for root stacks Cadman, Abramovich–Graber–Vistoli

ideas.what: The category of equivalences between (C_{A'},T_{A'}) and (C',T') is a bitorsor under the Picard categories of autoequivalences
ideas.modern_name: Bitorsors (Giraud), Morita bitorsors, gerbes of forms of a linear category
ideas.where_published: Giraud's book developed Grothendieck's ideas on torsors/gerbes

ideas.what: Unramified Dedekind categories have the equivalence category as a torsor under Tors(C', G_m)
ideas.modern_name: Azumaya algebras / Brauer class as a G_m-gerbe; twisted sheaves
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer I–III (Dix exposés), in algebra-level form

missed.claim: Grothendieck treats ramified orders categorically: an abstract A-linear 'Dedekind category' with ramification indices e_p and a Picard-type group whose quotient by Pic(A) is ⊕ Z/e_p. This is precisely the invariant later recovered by identifying hereditary orders with stacky curves / root stacks (Chan–Ingalls, Lieblich). It is an early categorical-stacky view of ramification of orders, in a motivic Galois context.
missed.quote: Ram(C/A) =def Pordet(C)/Pic(A) ≃ Σ_p Z/e_p(C)Z (e_p : degré de ramification)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests Grothendieck intended to allow ramified coefficient categories (not just Azumaya/Tannakian ones) in the Galois theory of motives over arithmetic bases. This prefigures noncommutative/stacky coefficient theories, and the link appears not to be credited to him.

missed.claim: The identification of the left and right torsor structures on the category of equivalences (unramified case) is left unverified. So is the general description of the band in the ramified case.
missed.quote: deux structures de tors-catégories s'identifient... (À vérifier !!)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small but explicit open point in a forms/descent theory for linear categories over Dedekind bases with ramification. Its ramified case would amount to a nonabelian H^1 of autoequivalence 2-groups of orders, rarely treated.

deep.surprise_reason: The bitorsor/Picard-category formalism is standard Grothendieck–Giraud. The abstract notion of a 'Dedekind category' with ramification group ⊕ Z/e_p, placed inside the motivic Galois program, is an unpublished and somewhat forward-looking detail. However, it is fragmentary and its content is classical for maximal orders.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely 'torseurs sur S de type fini, et on a π_1 s'inscrivant dans' (reading uncertain).
'Σ_p' should be read as a direct sum ⊕_p Z/e_p(C)Z.
In the margin hypothesis, '(C', A')' should read '(C', T')'; 'T' ∈ H_{A'}(C')' is a superscript insertion.
'voir A' local' is more likely 'p.ex. A' local'.
'Pordet' is an uncertain reading of Grothendieck's handwriting (possibly a Picard-type category name); treat it as tentative.
